small_guidance:
- The kernel only parallelizes over N tiles (single program per N column-block iterating all M=128); add a 2D grid over (M, N) with BLOCK_M=64 or 32 so multiple SMs share the work for each row group — currently with M=128 you launch only N/BLOCK_N programs (~128-256), leaving most of the 4090's 128 SMs idle.
- Add a GROUP_M swizzle (GROUP_M=8) over the 2D (pid_m, pid_n) grid for L2 reuse of the weight tiles, and broaden autotune to include BLOCK_M ∈ {32, 64, 128}, BLOCK_N ∈ {128, 256}, BLOCK_K ∈ {32, 64}, num_stages ∈ {3, 4, 5} — K=32768 is huge so deeper pipelining helps.
- Mask the tail K iterations only if K % BLOCK_K != 0 (here 32768 is divisible by all candidates, so keep the unmasked fast path) and ensure `tl.dot(..., allow_tf32=True)` / fp32 accumulator is explicit.
large_guidance:
- Redesign as a standard 2D persistent GEMM: grid = (cdiv(M, BLOCK_M) * cdiv(N, BLOCK_N),) with swizzled (pid_m, pid_n) decoding so all 128 SMs participate; current single-row-block design wastes ~75% of the GPU on this 128×32768×32768 problem.
- Consider splitting K across programs (split-K with atomic add or a second reduction pass) since K=32768 is very large and a single program serializes ~512-1024 K-iterations; a split-K of 2-4 ways combined with the (M,N) tiling should better fill the machine.
- Keep the bias + Swish + scale fused in the epilogue (already done) and store directly in fp32; alternatively store the pre-transposed weight in fp16/bf16 if accuracy permits to halve weight bandwidth (the kernel is heavily weight-bandwidth bound at 32k×32k).
